docs.title: Getting started
docs.description: Install the Howdy CLI and create your first Howdy project.

docs.title: Building a UI
docs.description: Build a themed page with Howdy UI, add a theme toggle, and bring it to life with a live component.

docs.title: Supervision and shutdown
docs.description: Run the server and everything else your app keeps alive under a supervisor, as an OTP application, so crashes are restarted and SIGTERM lets requests finish.

docs.title: Testing
docs.description: Test a Howdy app by sending it requests with howdy/testing, without starting a server.

docs.title: Username and password sign-in
docs.description: Add accounts to a Howdy app with Howdy Auth: register with a password, choose a unique username, and sign in with it.

docs.title: A console on your running app
docs.description: Attach a Gleam REPL to a running Howdy app with GSH, and call your code with the same database, auth and caches the server uses.

docs.title: The howdy command
docs.description: What the howdy command line does, what it needs, and how to run a project with howdy dev.

docs.title: Creating a project
docs.description: Create a Howdy project with howdy new, on SQLite, PostgreSQL or with no database.

docs.title: Generating code
docs.description: Generate JSON controllers, CRUD pages, repos and migrations for a Howdy project with howdy create.

docs.title: Router
docs.description: How Howdy matches requests to routes, and how to declare routes, parameters and wildcards.

docs.title: Path parameters
docs.description: Capture parts of the URL with :name and *name, and read them as typed values with howdy/param.

docs.title: Query strings
docs.description: Read typed values from the query string, with defaults, optional values and automatic 400 responses.

docs.title: Cookies
docs.description: Read, set and delete cookies, choose safe cookie options, and test handlers that use them.

docs.title: Forms
docs.description: Read JSON bodies, HTML forms and file uploads with howdy/body and howdy/form, validate the input, and report every field error.

docs.title: Responses
docs.description: Send text, HTML and JSON, set status codes and headers, and redirect from a Howdy handler.

docs.title: Guards
docs.description: Protect routes with guards that reject a request or hand the handler a typed value, such as the signed-in user.

docs.title: Services and errors
docs.description: Keep handlers lean by returning results from services, and learn the JSON shape of every Howdy error response.

docs.title: WebSockets
docs.description: Open WebSockets as ordinary routes, keep state per connection, broadcast to groups of sockets with channels, and track who is online with presence.

docs.title: Server-sent events
docs.description: Push events to browsers over an ordinary response with howdy/sse: broadcast to topics, resume after a reconnect, keep idle streams open, and test streams without a socket.

docs.title: Middleware
docs.description: Write middleware that rejects requests or changes responses, and attach it to an app, a controller or a route.

docs.title: Request logging
docs.description: Log the method, path and status of every request with the logger middleware.

docs.title: CORS
docs.description: Let pages on other origins call your Howdy API with the CORS middleware.

docs.title: CSRF protection
docs.description: Reject cross-site writes to a cookie-authenticated app with the CSRF middleware, which checks the Origin header and needs no tokens.

docs.title: Rate limiting
docs.description: Cap how fast clients can make requests with fixed window and token bucket rate limits.

docs.title: API versioning
docs.description: Serve several versions of an API side by side with version groups, fallback and a choice of versioning strategy.

docs.title: Howdy Database
docs.description: Install the optional howdy_database package, and open SQLite or PostgreSQL with safe defaults.

docs.title: Transactions and queries
docs.description: Run queries and transactions that behave the same on PostgreSQL and SQLite, and turn constraint violations into errors.

docs.title: Migrations
docs.description: Create and upgrade your own tables with checksummed, package-owned migrations, and check the schema at startup.

docs.title: Howdy Mail
docs.description: Install the optional howdy_mail package, write messages with smail templates, and send them with a mailer.

docs.title: Adapters
docs.description: Send mail over SMTP, Resend or SendGrid, redirect it on staging, fall back to a second provider, or write your own adapter.

docs.title: Outbox and previews
docs.description: Keep mail in an outbox while you develop, read it and preview your templates in the admin area, and check it in tests.

docs.title: Howdy Auth
docs.description: Install the optional howdy_auth package, create its tables, mount its routes and protect your own with its guard.

docs.title: Social sign-in
docs.description: Sign people in with Google, Apple, GitHub, Facebook or Microsoft Entra, and link those accounts to existing users.

docs.title: Passkeys
docs.description: Sign in and register with passkeys, offer them in the browser's autofill, and share them across subdomains.

docs.title: Multi-factor authentication
docs.description: Ask for a second factor after every sign-in: authenticator apps, delivered codes, recovery codes and remembered devices.

docs.title: Enterprise single sign-on
docs.description: Connect each customer's own identity provider over OpenID Connect or SAML, and require it for their staff.

docs.title: Signing in
docs.description: Sign visitors in with emailed tokens: sending the email, the JSON API, browser cookies, bearer tokens and headless operations.

docs.title: Passwords
docs.description: Turn on password sign-in, and learn how passwords are registered, reset, checked, rate limited and stored.

docs.title: Sessions and policy
docs.description: List and revoke sessions, renew them while in use, sign in to several accounts at once, and keep sessions in an external store.

docs.title: Account changes
docs.description: Let users change their email address, unlink providers and delete their account.

docs.title: Groups
docs.description: Put users in workspaces or tenants with groups, and choose whether an email address has one account or one per group.

docs.title: Fields
docs.description: Keep small typed facts about users and groups, such as a unique username, without a table of your own.

docs.title: Roles and permissions
docs.description: Define roles, grant them to users globally or per organization, and check permissions from a guard.

docs.title: Migrations
docs.description: Run the package's checksummed migrations, add tables of your own alongside them, and understand the startup schema check.

docs.title: User administration
docs.description: Provision, suspend and resume users from trusted code, read the audit trail, and set client limits behind a proxy.

docs.title: Howdy Admin
docs.description: Mount the development admin area from dev/, choose what it shows, and keep it away from anyone else.

docs.title: Database browser
docs.description: Search, filter, sort and edit your tables in a grid that follows the database as it changes, on PostgreSQL or SQLite.

docs.title: Users and roles
docs.description: Create, suspend and delete users, revoke their sessions, manage groups and roles, and sign in to your app as any user.

docs.title: Telemetry
docs.description: See each request as a timeline of its queries, calls, emails and logs, with repeated and slow queries pointed out.

docs.title: Calling your API
docs.description: Browse the endpoints of your OpenAPI document and call them from the admin, anonymously or signed in as any user.

docs.title: Remote calls
docs.description: Define typed procedures once, serve them from one Howdy service and call them from another with howdy_remote.

docs.title: Clusters and security
docs.description: Run services as an Erlang cluster, call across a trust boundary over HTTP, and call plain Erlang and Elixir nodes.

docs.title: OpenAPI documents
docs.description: Document a JSON API as OpenAPI 3.1 with howdy_openapi, from endpoints that read their inputs through schemas, and serve an interactive reference.

docs.title: Schemas
docs.description: Describe a JSON value once and get its decoder, its encoder and its JSON Schema, with constraints checked while decoding.

docs.title: Telemetry
docs.description: Switch on OpenTelemetry: send traces to a collector in production, or record them for the admin in development.

docs.title: Tracing
docs.description: The spans Howdy opens for requests, queries, remote calls, email and sign-in, and how to add your own.

docs.title: Logs
docs.description: Tie log lines to their traces, record crashes, and write logs as JSON with trace ids.

docs.title: Pages
docs.description: Render whole HTML documents with howdy/ui/page, with the theme and styles in place before first paint.

docs.title: Components
docs.description: The ready-made Howdy UI components: headings, text, buttons, form fields and layout.

docs.title: Themes
docs.description: Define light, dark and brand themes as Gleam records, and let visitors switch between them.

docs.title: Custom components
docs.description: Copy a built-in Howdy UI component to change it, or write your own from theme tokens.

docs.title: Live components
docs.description: Run interactive Lustre components on the server over a WebSocket, and move between live pages without a reload, with no JavaScript to write.

docs.title: Publishing
docs.description: Serve Howdy UI styles as one cacheable CSS file, in development and when published.
